facts.statement: Mandasuchus lived during the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic in Tanzania.
facts.quote: Mandasuchus is an extinct genus of loricatan pseudosuchian from the Manda Formation of Tanzania, which dates back to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Mandasuchus was a quadrupedal carnivore that possessed a relatively long neck.
facts.quote: It was a quadrupedal carnivore with a relatively long neck.

facts.statement: The genus Mandasuchus was first mentioned by Alan Charig in 1956 but was not formally described until 2018.
facts.quote: Although this genus was first mentioned by Alan Charig in 1956, a formal description was not published until 2018.

facts.statement: Richard J. Butler and colleagues formally described Mandasuchus in 2018 following a multinational study of Triassic rift fossils in Tanzania and Zambia.
facts.quote: Mandasuchus was finally formally described in 2018 by Richard J. Butler and colleagues, as part of a multinational investigation into the fossils of Triassic rift systems in Tanzania and Zambia.

facts.statement: Several well-preserved specimens of Mandasuchus have been discovered, but cranial material is scarce.
facts.quote: Several well preserved specimens have been found, although there is little cranial material.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis classifies Mandasuchus as a loricatan that is more basal than Prestosuchus and distinct from, though closely related to, Ticinosuchus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis recovered it as a loricatan more basal than Prestosuchus and not synonymous with Ticinosuchus, albeit not too distantly related either.

facts.statement: The single preserved tooth of Mandasuchus is thin and serrated.
facts.quote: The only preserved tooth is thin and serrated.

facts.statement: The longest cervical vertebrae of Mandasuchus have a centrum that is approximately 1.8 times longer than it is high.
facts.quote: The centrum (main spool-shaped component) of Mandasuchus's longest cervical (neck) vertebrae are about 1.8 times longer than high.

facts.statement: Mandasuchus had two rows of staggered osteoderms along its back, creating asymmetrical armor.
facts.quote: Osteoderms (bony plates) extended down the back in two rows which were "staggered". i.e. offset from each other so that the armor is asymmetrical.

facts.statement: Mandasuchus possessed a crocodile-normal or crurotarsal ankle structure where a peg on the astragalus fits into a pit on the calcaneum.
facts.quote: Mandasuchus has a "crocodile-normal" or "crurotarsal" ankle, with a prominent peg on the astragalus fitting into a shallower pit on the calcaneum.

facts.statement: Mandasuchus is classified within the unranked order Crurotarsi.
Mandasuchus belongs to the unranked family Paracrocodylomorpha.
J. Michael Parrish debated whether Mandasuchus was a distinct genus, proposing it was synonymous with Ticinosuchus ferox based on similar postcranial bones until a formal description was published.
facts.quote: J. Michael Parrish argued that Mandasuchus was not a distinct genus. He proposed that it was in the same genus as the European archosaur Ticinosuchus ferox due to the similarity of some homologous postcranial bones, but withheld final taxonomic determination of Mandasuchus until Charig provided a published description of the material.

facts.statement: A 1965 study suggested Mandasuchus was a possible ancestor of prosauropods, though this hypothesis lacked explanation and is now considered highly improbable.
facts.quote: Charig y dos coautores sugirieron en un estudio de 1965 que trataba sobre los saurisquios que "Mandasuchus" era un posible ancestro de los prosaurópodos, aunque no se dio ninguna explicación para esa afirmación, que se considera en todo caso muy improbable.

rejected.statement: The skull of Mandasuchus features a low maxilla with an elongated antorbital fenestra and at least 12 tooth sockets separated by interdental plates.
rejected.quote: The maxilla is low, with an elongated antorbital fenestra and at least 12 tooth sockets separated by discrete interdental plates.

rejected.statement: The femur of Mandasuchus possesses a distinct oval pit on its rear edge, a feature not found in other pseudosuchians.
